items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Advanced degree in Student Affairs/Higher Education or another related field.
Dust: Yes
4-7 of related experience.
Experience living, working or and/or studying abroad.
Experience working with international students and scholars; demonstrated knowledge of their adjustment and support needs.
Demonstrated experience in programming and event coordination/management.
Experience developing, facilitating and evaluating support programs, intercultural training and orientation programs for international students or scholars.

The ISS program coordinator is responsible for the development, delivery and review of programs, projects and events that create community, celebrate culture and promote global engagement. The program coordinator assumes the primary responsibility for the overall management and coordination of International Student Orientation. This includes conducting research, designing, marketing, and assisting in the execution of Orientation and other adjustment and support programs that cater to the needs of UCR’s undergraduate and graduate international students. Additionally, they serve as the primary logistics coordinator for ISS, facilitating program meetings and events, and co-managing the departments newsletter and social media presence. The coordinator is also responsible for designing and coordinating community-building events for students and scholars. Works directly with the scholar team to plan and execute scholar focused events. Federal regulations mandate that sponsoring institutions provide regular orientation, informational, and cultural sessions to F-1 and J-1 students and scholars. The program coordinator is accountable for ensuring the fulfillment of these obligations. (20% time)

Guides students and scholars on complex and sensitive matters relating to cultural adjustment and intercultural communication. Coaches students and scholars to plan events and projects that foster the success and well-being of our international community. Facilitates student-led workshops on international student success. (15% time)
Manage peer mentoring programs, orientation leaders, event coordinators, and volunteers to include: recruitment, hiring, onboarding, training, and supervision. (15% time)

Maintains relationships with internal and external organization stakeholders critical to program success. Works with community and campus partners to coordinate programs and organize cultural events. Maintains communication and effective relationships with colleagues and departments to enhance the international student and scholar experience and build community. In collaboration with others, plans and implements an outreach strategy targeting both on-campus and off-campus supporters to raise awareness of international student and scholar support programs and needs. (10% time)

Provides recommendations, reports, and metrics on the feasibility of new and current programs. Devises preferred program learning and service outcomes, creates measures to assess effectiveness, and makes recommendations for changes/new programs and services. Expands and enhances programs and services designed to promote community building, intercultural communication skills, and a mutual exchange of culture, language, and learning across campus. (10% time)

Provides support to international students to facilitate the academic and socio-cultural adjustment to campus, including matters related to pre-arrival, arrival and adjustment to the United States. Makes appropriate referrals to campus partners. (10% time)

In collaboration with leadership, proposes a budget for yearly programming events and works within that approved budget to execute events. Works closely with the administrative team to request the hiring and onboarding of student employees and volunteers, and to request room reservations, catering, and the purchase of other required materials for program execution. (10% time)
May serve as a back up Designated School Official during peak periods with minor immigration matters, such as travel signatures. (5% time)
Additional duties as assigned. (5% time)
